title: Emergency follow-up: rate-tier misattribution during traffic-shaper rollout caused regional 429 surge
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of the new traffic-shaper configuration (traffic-shaper v2) we observed a regional surge of 429 responses that lasted ~47 minutes across two east-coast datacenters. The canary policy incorrectly mapped several enterprise and free-tier rate-tiers to the same enforcement bucket due to a translation bug in the rollout propagation service. This caused aggressive token draining for many customers and triggered client-side retries that amplified the storm. This ticket captures the root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and the follow-up action plan to prevent recurrence.
impact: ~14% of hosted API requests in region-us-east received 429s; several production customers reported degraded user experiences and temporary elevated latency as clients retried. Estimated revenue-impact window: 47 minutes. No data loss or security exposure.
timeline: 2025-02-10 03:12 UTC - Canary rollout of traffic-shaper v2 started (10% of traffic in us-east-1 and us-east-2).
2025-02-10 03:18 UTC - Monitoring triggered alerts: 429 rate increased and per-token latency rose above SLO in us-east clusters.
2025-02-10 03:20 UTC - On-call rotated to SRE + API gateway squad. Initial mitigation: paused canary rollout at control-plane layer.
2025-02-10 03:24 UTC - Hot rollback executed: traffic-shaper config reverted to v1 across affected regions. 429 rate began to decline.
2025-02-10 03:59 UTC - 429s returned to baseline; post-incident notification sent to impacted customers and internal stakeholders.
2025-02-10 04:30 UTC - Post-incident conference: decision to open full RCA and block any further traffic-shaper rollouts until verification harness is added.
2025-02-12 10:00 UTC - Initial RCA draft completed; assigned action items and owners.
2025-02-24 09:00 UTC - Patch for propagation-service translation and additional integration tests merged to staging.
root_cause: A data-mapping regression in the rollout propagation service incorrectly collapsed new rate-tier identifiers when applying the canary policy. Specifically, a normalization function designed to de-duplicate legacy tier aliases inadvertently normalized distinct new tier IDs into the same enforcement key because of a short-circuit in the alias-to-bucket mapping. This manifested only in canary mode because the canary path uses a simplified propagation endpoint that accidentally skipped a namespacing header. Two contributing factors: insufficient canary-path test coverage and lack of guardrails that validate per-tier traffic distribution during rollouts.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of traffic-shaper v2 canary (completed 2025-02-10 03:24 UTC)
Emergency patch to propagation service to preserve namespace header and stop alias normalization shortcut (hotfix deployed to prod 2025-02-11)
Disabled simplified canary endpoint until tests and validation added
Customer communication sent with incident summary and remediation steps
action_items: ENG: Add end-to-end canary validation tests that assert per-rate-tier traffic distribution and enforcement buckets (owner: Ethan Park) - due 2025-03-07
SRE: Instrument real-time per-tier heatmaps in the console and add alerting when a single enforcement bucket receives >120% of expected tier traffic (owner: Sofia Alvarez) - due 2025-03-03
ENG: Harden propagation-service: remove alias normalization short-circuit and add unit tests covering legacy alias edge-cases (owner: Noah Brooks) - due 2025-02-28
ENG: Add a rollout guard that prevents more than 1% of production traffic from being mapped to a single enforcement bucket during canaries (owner: Maya Rivera) - due 2025-03-05
Product: Update rollout playbook to require a pre-rollout tier distribution report and sign-off for any rate-tier or billing-related config changes (owner: Priya Singh) - due 2025-03-10
Support: Follow-up outreach to top 10 impacted customers with tailored remediation notes and credit offers (owner: Carlos Mendes) - due 2025-02-20 (completed)
verification_plan: Validation will include: (1) running the new e2e canary validation harness in staging and canary before any new traffic-shaper rollouts; (2) a scheduled small-scale canary (0.5% traffic) with per-tier heatmap verification for two weekly rollouts; (3) automated gating that fails rollouts if any bucket exceeds the 120% threshold. Success criteria: zero tier-collapsing regressions in three consecutive canaries and no detected per-tier skew after 72 hours of rollout in prod.
notes: We observed amplified client retries from SDK versions < 2.3.1; recommend adding a client-strategy advisory in SDK release notes.
This edge-case did not affect Dedicated customers using per-tenant enforcement paths because those bypass the simplified canary endpoint.
Consider an automated teardown that reverses partial propagation if the propagation service returns a schema-validation warning during rollout.
